title: OpenCLI Specification
description: A JSON Schema specification for defining command-line interfaces. Inspired by OpenAPI, OpenCLI enables code generation, documentation, help-text and shell completions from a single declarative source.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to the OpenCLI JSON Schema, used by editors for validation and completion.

opencli.description: The OpenCLI specification version this document conforms to. Uses semantic versioning.

commands.description: The top-level commands exposed by the CLI.

flags.description: Global flags available to all commands. These are inherited by every command and subcommand unless overridden.

exitCodes.description: Program-wide exit codes and their meanings. Individual commands may add or refine entries via their own exitCodes. Zero conventionally means success; non-zero indicates a specific failure mode.

components.description: Reusable components that can be referenced across the spec.

CommandOrReference.description: Either an inline Command or a $ref to a reusable one. The presence of '$ref' selects the branch, so validation errors come from only the relevant shape.

FlagOrReference.description: Either an inline Flag or a $ref to a reusable one.

ArgumentOrReference.description: Either an inline Argument or a $ref to a reusable one.

ExampleOrReference.description: Either an inline Example or a $ref to a reusable one.

title.description: The name of the CLI tool. Used in generated help headers and documentation titles.

version.description: The version of the CLI tool itself (not the spec version).

description.description: A short description of the CLI tool. Appears in --help output and documentation.

longDescription.description: A detailed, multi-paragraph description. Used in man pages and extended documentation. Supports Markdown.

homepage.description: URL to the project homepage or repository.

documentationUrl.description: URL to web-based documentation. Generators may surface this in --help and man pages so users can link to and search the full docs online.

binaryName.description: The executable name as invoked from the shell. Defaults to info.title if omitted.

name.description: Identifying name of the contact person or organization.
SPDX license expression or license name.

url.description: URL to the full license text.

name.description: The command name as typed on the command line. Must be a single word with no spaces. Use kebab-case for multi-word commands.

aliases.description: Alternative names that invoke the same command.

description.description: A concise, one-line description. Shown in command listings and --help summaries.

longDescription.description: A detailed description. Shown when running <cmd> --help. Supports Markdown.

usage.description: A custom usage line. If omitted, one is auto-generated from the command name, flags, and arguments.

hidden.description: When true, the command is excluded from --help listings and completions but remains functional if invoked directly.

deprecated.description: When true, a deprecation warning is emitted when the command is used.

deprecationMessage.description: A message explaining the deprecation and suggesting an alternative.

arguments.description: Positional arguments for this command. Order matters.

commands.description: Subcommands nested under this command. Each subcommand is itself a full Command, so nesting is recursive to any depth.

envVars.description: Environment variables that affect this command's behavior.

tags.description: Categorization labels for grouping commands in documentation.

exitCodes.description: Exit codes this command can return, mapped to their failure modes. Augments or refines any program-wide exitCodes.

flagGroups.description: Constraints across this command's flags, such as mutual exclusivity or co-requirement. Used to generate validation and to document the relationships.

stdin.description: Describes whether and how this command consumes standard input (piped data, or a flag/argument value of '-').

output.description: Describes the command's output: the formats it can emit, which flag selects the format, and the structure of machine-readable formats.

name.description: The long-form flag name, without leading dashes. Used as --<name>.

short.description: The short-form flag, a single character without the leading dash. Used as -<short>.

description.description: A concise description shown in --help next to the flag.

longDescription.description: Extended description for documentation. Supports Markdown.

type.description: The data type of the flag value.

default.description: The default value when the flag is not provided. Must match the declared flag type.

required.description: When true, the flag must be provided or a default must exist.

deprecated.description: When true, a deprecation warning is emitted when the flag is used.

deprecationMessage.description: A message explaining the deprecation and suggesting an alternative.

hidden.description: When true, the flag is excluded from --help but remains functional.

envVar.description: An environment variable that can supply the flag value when the flag is not provided.

choices.description: Allowed values for this flag. The flag value must be one of these. Used for validation and shell completions.

placeholder.description: A placeholder name shown in help text to indicate the expected value format.

repeatable.description: When true, the flag can be specified multiple times. Values are collected into a list.

count.description: When true, the flag acts as a counter (e.g., -v, -vv, -vvv). Implies type: integer. Cannot be combined with repeatable.

sensitive.description: When true, the flag carries a secret such as a password, token, or key. Reading secrets directly from flags is discouraged (they leak into process listings and shell history), so generators should prefer a companion file or stdin (e.g. a --password-file flag) and must never echo the value.

FlagType.description:
Allowed data types for flag and argument values. Each type has exactly one canonical spelling.

- string: arbitrary text
- integer: whole numbers
- number: decimal numbers
- boolean: true/false flags (no value needed)
- duration: time spans like '5m', '1h30s'
- file: a path to a file (supports '-' for stdin/stdout)
- path: a filesystem path to a file or directory
- url: a valid URI
- email: an email address

Values restricted to a fixed set are expressed with `choices` on the flag or argument, not a dedicated enum type.

name.description: The argument name. Shown in usage as <NAME> or [NAME].

description.description: A description of what this argument represents.

type.description: The data type of the argument value.

required.description: When true, this argument must be provided. Required arguments must precede optional ones.

default.description: Default value when the argument is not provided and not required.

variadic.description: When true, this argument consumes all remaining positional values (like ...rest). Must be the last argument.

placeholder.description: Custom placeholder text in usage line. Overrides the default <NAME> format.

command.description: The full command line invocation, including the binary name.

description.description: A brief explanation of what this example demonstrates.

output.description: Expected output from running the example command. Useful for documentation.

default.description: Default value if the environment variable is not set.

ExitCode.description: An exit status the program or command can return, mapped to a failure mode.

code.description: The numeric exit status. Zero conventionally indicates success; non-zero indicates a specific failure mode.

label.description: A short symbolic name for the exit code, suitable for generating a named constant.

description.description: What this exit code means. Surfaced in documentation and man pages.

FlagGroup.description: A constraint across a set of flags. Maps directly to parser features such as Cobra's MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive / MarkFlagsRequiredTogether / MarkFlagsOneRequired.

type.description:
The kind of relationship:

- mutuallyExclusive: at most one of the flags may be set.
- requiredTogether: if any flag in the group is set, all of them must be set.
- oneRequired: at least one of the flags must be set.

flags.description: The long-form names of the flags participating in this group.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the constraint, for documentation.

StdinSpec.description: Describes a command's use of standard input.

description.description: What the command reads from stdin and in what shape.

required.description: When true, the command expects data on stdin. If stdin is an interactive terminal, the command should display help and exit rather than hang.

format.description: The expected input format, used for documentation and validation hints.

OutputSpec.description: Describes a command's output. Text is the default for most tools, but many now emit structured formats (JSON, YAML) or Markdown. When a format is structured, its `schema` captures the shape of the data so generators can produce output types/structs and documentation.

formatFlag.description: The long-form name of the flag that selects the output format on this command (e.g. 'output' for --output, 'format' for --format). The flag's `choices` should correspond to the declared format values. Omit for commands with a single fixed format.

formats.description: The output formats this command can produce. The format marked `default: true` is emitted when the format flag is absent.

OutputFormat.description: A single output format a command can emit.

format.description: Identifier for this format. Common values: text, markdown, json, yaml, table, csv, tsv, ndjson, none. Open-ended, since tools invent their own (e.g. kubectl's 'wide', 'jsonpath', 'go-template').

value.description: The value passed to the format-selecting flag to choose this format. Defaults to `format` when omitted (e.g. --output=json).

description.description: What this format produces and when to use it.

default.description: When true, this format is used when the format flag is not provided. At most one format per command should be marked default.

schema.description: A JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) describing the structure of this format's output. Meaningful for structured formats (json, yaml, ndjson). May use a standard JSON Schema `$ref` to point into '#/components/schemas/...' for reuse. Generators use this to emit output types/structs and to document the response shape.

Reference.description: A reference to a reusable component defined under the top-level `components` object. The pointer is a JSON Pointer into this document, e.g. '#/components/flags/verbose'.

$ref.description: JSON Pointer to a component, such as '#/components/flags/output' or '#/components/commands/login'.

Components.description: Reusable component definitions that can be referenced via $ref elsewhere in the spec.

flags.description: Reusable flag definitions keyed by a unique identifier.

arguments.description: Reusable argument definitions keyed by a unique identifier.

commands.description: Reusable command definitions keyed by a unique identifier.

examples.description: Reusable example definitions keyed by a unique identifier.

schemas.description: Reusable JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) definitions for structured output types and complex flag/argument values. Reference them with a standard JSON Schema `$ref`, e.g. '#/components/schemas/Pod'.
